Harold Padilla’s knowledge in scenario 2 is limited to what he has experienced or been told up to that point. He knows:

- He felt frustrated and anxious about his project team’s motivation in scenario 1.
- He met Arthur and received Arthur’s advice: understand team members’ individual motivations and have one-on-one conversations.
- After talking with Arthur, Harold feels hopeful and relieved.
- Harold believes Arthur’s advice will be helpful.
- Harold decides/intends to implement that advice in his team meetings.
- In scenario 2, he acts on that intention by telling the team he wants to try one-on-one chats and by saying he will schedule time with each member.
- He hears Team Member 1 and Team Member 2 respond positively or openly.

Harold does not know, at this point, the later events from scenarios 3–5: that the team will still not respond well, that deeper issues such as tension or workload stress exist, or that he will later investigate conflicts and introduce feedback sessions and team-building activities. Those events are objective story events but are not yet known to Harold in scenario 2.

The question asks how Harold’s intention in scenario 2 influences his action. In scenario 2, Harold’s intention is to use Arthur’s advice by implementing it with his team. This intention leads directly to his action of introducing one-on-one conversations in the team meeting and planning to schedule individual chats. This matches choice f.

ANSWER: f
